newsitem.title: UK: Moscow Eurobond due in first quarter 1997 -dealers.
newsitem.headline: Moscow Eurobond due in first quarter 1997 -dealers.

text.p: Moscow city's debut Eurobond is expected to be launched in late February or early March, bankers familiar with the deal said on Tuesday.
The size could be for up to $500 million and a three- or five-year maturity was being considered, they said.
"Moscow's borrowing plans are on target at the moment, with launch due in late February or maybe early March," said an official at a bank involved in the transaction.
"They will be doing their due diligence next week, and after that make definite plans," he said.
Credit Suisse First Boston and Nomura were appointed to lead manage Moscow's debut international bond issue.
Earlier, Moscow officials said they had met representatives from Moody's on Monday in the first of a series of talks ahead of the Eurobond launch. Other rating agencies will be met too, they said.
Last November Russia tapped the international bond markets for the first time since the 1917 revolution with a $1.0 billion five-year transaction.
Priced to yield 345 basis points over U.S. Treasury bonds, the deal was now trading at around 400 b.p. over.
This spread widening would affect Moscow's decision on what maturity to tap, traders said.
"If Moscow launches a five-year deal the spread will be compared with that on the Russia paper," said an emerging market debt trader.
"A three-year maturity would be better because there is no comparable sovereign paper. Instead, it might be compared with the three-year Kazakhstan issue which has traded well," he said.
Kazakhstan launched at $200 million three-year bond in December at 350 b.p. over U.S. Treasury notes. It was quoted at 307 b.p. over on the bid side on Tuesday.
Elsewhere, Russia's second city of St Petersburg was reported to be planning a $100 million debut bond for launch at the end of this month or early February.
The official Itar-Tass news agency said on Tuesday St Petersburg's mayor said the deal would have a two- to five-year maturity and would be followed by a $300 million issue.
Salomon Brothers will lead manage the deal.
